post.description: Proves control of the CURRENT number and reserves the new one. Requires a Firebase ID token minted for the current number within the last 300 seconds. Returns a single-use challenge that expires in 600 seconds and is redeemed by POST /api/v1/auth/phone-change/complete. Gated by PHONE_CHANGE_ENABLED.

new_phone.description: The number to move the account to. Must differ from the current number and must not belong to another active account.

id_token.description: Firebase ID token proving control of the CURRENT number, minted within the last 300 seconds.

challenge_token.description: Single-use secret. Stored only as a hash; it is not retrievable after this response.

400.description: The new number is not a valid E.164 number, or is the current number.

value.title: New Phone Mismatch
value.detail: new_phone must be a valid E.164 number different from the current one.

401.description: Missing credentials, or the proof of the current number is absent, stale or for a different identity.

value.title: Current Proof Mismatch
value.detail: The supplied token does not prove recent control of the current number.

403.description: The account is suspended or banned.

value.title: Account Restricted
value.detail: This account cannot perform the operation.

409.description: The requested number already belongs to another active account.

value.title: Phone Already Used
value.detail: That number is already in use.

value.title: Rate Limited
value.detail: Too many requests.

503.description: PHONE_CHANGE_ENABLED is false, or the identity provider is not configured.

value.title: Phone Change Disabled
value.detail: Phone change is closed in this environment.

post.description: Redeems the challenge with a Firebase ID token proving control of the NEW number, re-points the identity and rewrites the account's phone. Every registered device is deleted and every outstanding step-up proof is revoked, so the caller must supply the device secret it wants to keep using. Single use: a redeemed challenge answers 409.

challenge_token.description: The single-use token returned when the challenge was opened.

replacement_device_secret.description: The device secret to install for this device. Every previously registered device is revoked, so without this the caller signs itself out.

id_token.description: Firebase ID token proving control of the NEW number, minted within the last 300 seconds.

200.description: The account's number was changed and all prior devices were revoked.

prior_devices_revoked.description: Always true. Every other device must re-authenticate.

400.description: The challenge is unknown, belongs to another seller, or a required field is missing.

value.title: Invalid Challenge
value.detail: The challenge could not be redeemed.

401.description: Missing credentials, or the proof of the new number is absent, stale or for a different number.

value.title: New Phone Mismatch
value.detail: The supplied token does not prove recent control of the new number.

403.description: The account is suspended or banned.

value.title: Account Restricted
value.detail: This account cannot perform the operation.

409.description: The challenge was already redeemed, or the number was taken in the meantime.

value.title: Replayed Challenge
value.detail: This challenge has already been used.

410.description: The challenge expired. Open a new one.

value.title: Expired Challenge
value.detail: The challenge is older than 600 seconds.

value.title: Rate Limited
value.detail: Too many requests.

503.description: PHONE_CHANGE_ENABLED is false, or the identity provider is not configured.

value.title: Phone Change Disabled
value.detail: Phone change is closed in this environment.

post.summary: Record an order taken outside the storefront
post.description:
Creates an order the seller took in a conversation, in the shop, or over the phone. It is the same order as one placed on the storefront: same validation, same monthly plan limit, same per-store order number sequence, and the same stock movement. Only the origin differs, which is recorded on the row.

The app writes the order locally first so recording it does not depend on a signal, then posts it here. Until this call succeeds the order is not on the account: it does not reach a second device, does not survive a reinstall, is not counted against the plan, and cannot be advanced through its pipeline.

idempotency_key.description: Required, and owned by the client. Unlike the storefront, which mints one when a browser sends none, this route refuses to invent it: the app records orders offline and retries them on the next sync, so a retry after a dropped response is the normal case and a key generated per attempt would make each retry a new order. Reuse the same key for the same order and the existing order is returned.

buyer_phone.description: 8 to 15 digits. Non-digits are stripped before validation.

product_code.description: The product's immutable public code. Must belong to this store.

items.description: Every product must be in stock for the quantity asked; the whole order is refused otherwise.

pay_method.description: A transfer method is only accepted when the store has published a handle for it.

200.description: The order is on the account. Also returned for a replayed key, with replayed: true and no second order written.

order_no.description: The per-store order number. Store it as the order's remote id: it is what PATCH /api/v1/orders/{order_no}/status addresses, and the number the seller reads aloud.

total_minor.description: Computed from the store's own prices, not from the request.

currency.description: One currency per order; a mixed-currency order is refused.

replayed.description: True when this key had already been used and no new order was written.

400.description: idempotency_key is missing or malformed, the buyer phone or item list is invalid, a product code does not belong to this store, the same product appears twice, or the payment method is not one the store has published.

value.title: Idempotency Key Required
value.detail: Send idempotency_key: 8-100 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._:-].

value.title: Unauthorized
value.detail: Seller credentials are required.

403.description: The store is not accepting orders, or the buyer is restricted.

value.title: Orders Disabled
value.detail: This store is not accepting orders.

409.description: The order could not be written as asked: stock_changed when a line exceeds what is in stock, mixed_currency_order when the lines are not all in one currency, or plan_limit_reached at the monthly order limit.

value.title: Stock Changed
value.detail: One or more products no longer have the stock requested.

value.title: Rate Limited
value.detail: Too many requests.

503.description: Writes for this store are fenced, during a tenant shard migration. Retryable: the response carries retry-after and the order has not been written.

value.title: Tenant Write Fenced
value.detail: Writes for this store are paused. Retry after the interval given.

post.description: Mirrors the seller catalog. Products absent from the submitted array are deleted, so `products` is required: omitting it is rejected rather than treated as an empty catalog. An explicitly empty array is honoured and clears the catalog.

products.description: The complete catalog as the client holds it. Anything omitted here is deleted server-side. Omitting the field entirely is rejected with 400 products_required — it is never read as an empty catalog. Each product identifies itself with remote_uuid, the id this endpoint returned when it first accepted the product; omit it (or send null) only for a product that has never synced. app_id is the client's own row id: it is echoed back so the client can find its local row, and it is used to match an existing product only for a product that sent no remote_uuid and whose number no other row in the request has already claimed — two devices number different products alike, and matching on it overwrote one with the other.

baseline_version.description: The catalog_version this device last downloaded from GET /api/v1/products. Required for any push that modifies or deletes an existing product: the endpoint is a full mirror, so an omission is a deletion, and a device that has not downloaded cannot tell the server that the seller has no products apart from the fact that it has not looked. Omit it only for a purely additive push, which cannot destroy what it has never seen. A value that no longer matches the store is refused with 409 stale_catalog.

confirm_deletion.description: Required when the push deletes at least half of a catalog of ten or more products. A current baseline proves the device has seen what it is deleting; it does not prove the seller meant to.

valid.summary: Full mirror of a one-product catalog that has synced before

empty_catalog.summary: Seller has deleted every product; the empty array is explicit

second_device.summary: A second phone pushes the product it downloaded plus one it invented offline

products.description: One entry per product in the request, in the order it was sent.

catalog_version.description: The store's catalog version after this write. Send it as baseline_version on the next push: an accepted push moves the version, so the baseline just used is spent.

count.description: How many submitted products the store now holds.

patch.summary: Advance an order through its pipeline
patch.description:
Moves one order to the next state, or cancels it. The server owns the transition table: NEW -> CONFIRMED -> PAID -> SHIPPED -> DONE, with CANCELLED reachable only from NEW or CONFIRMED, and DONE and CANCELLED terminal. Any other move is refused with 409 rather than applied.

Requesting the status an order already holds succeeds with `changed: false`, so a client retrying a dropped response converges instead of showing an error for work that landed.

Cancelling returns the reserved stock to the catalog. Placing the order took it, and until this operation existed nothing gave it back.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The per-store order number (`order_no` from GET /api/v1/orders), not the UUID. It is unique per store and this operation is scoped to one store by authentication, so it identifies exactly one order.

status.description: Target state. NEW is not accepted: an order starts there and never returns.

changed.description: False when the order already held the requested status.

order_no.description: The per-store order number that was addressed.

Money.description: An amount in the currency's minor units, plus the currency. The number of minor units per major unit follows ISO 4217 and is not always 100: EGP has 2 decimal places, KWD has 3. Never divide by a constant.

Product.description: One product as the store holds it. Identified by remote_uuid: app_id is the row id on whichever device first pushed it and means nothing on any other device, and product_code is the public, shareable code.

app_id.description: The store's internal numbering for this product, seeded from the row id of the device that created it. Not an identity: two devices number different products alike, so a client must match on remote_uuid.

remote_uuid.description: The server's id for this product. Store it with the local row and send it back on every push — it is the only value that means the same product on every device.

SyncedProductIdentity.description: The identity the server assigned to one submitted product. Exactly one entry per product in the request — never the rest of the store, whose app_ids belong to other devices and would collide with the caller's own row ids.

app_id.description: Echoed exactly as it was sent, so the device can find the local row this entry describes.

remote_uuid.description: The server's id for this product. Persist it: sending it on the next push is what stops a second device's product being filed as an edit of this one.
